METADATA.title: Should I Restore My Vintage Guitar Before Selling It?
METADATA.description: Get your vintage guitar assessed before paying for repairs or restoration. I'll explain repair costs, originality and when work may be necessary.

mainEntity.name: Should I Clean Or Restring The Guitar Before An Appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Leave the surface, strings and parts as they are for the initial assessment. Clear photographs and an accurate description are more useful than cosmetic preparation.

mainEntity.name: Will A New Finish Help It Sell For More?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full refinish generally means 40 to 60 percent less than a comparable original. Don't repaint a vintage guitar to prepare it for sale before its current finish and condition have been assessed.

mainEntity.name: Should I Pay For A Neck Reset Before Selling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Get an assessment first. A proper reset carries almost no penalty, but you still need to compare the actual repair quote with the realistic sale options for the guitar as it stands.

mainEntity.name: What If The Bridge Is Lifting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for handling advice promptly. If you can safely loosen the strings without stressing the damaged area, relieve the tension. Don't press the bridge down, test the gap or apply glue; stop if handling or the tuners appear unsafe.

mainEntity.name: What If I Already Had The Guitar Restored?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep the invoices and removed parts, and describe the work plainly. An assessment can establish the instrument's current condition and the right comparison without pretending the changes never happened.
